title: Choose the bolder Tokens page direction
question: This hand moves beyond the reference-sheet layout while staying inside FDS's compact, operational visual system.

options.label: The token switchboard
options.thesis: Five real UI needs become live routes from intent to the correct token layer.
options.viewport: A full-width decision board runs five example requests through Intent, Use, and Owner columns; the active Route Blue line makes the answer traceable in one glance.
options.risk: It only works if the scenarios stay real and few, not a decorative flowchart.

options.label: The layer cross-section
options.thesis: The system is explained as three connected layers, not three isolated documentation sections.
options.viewport: Three wide horizontal bands fill the opening: Primitive feeds Semantic, Semantic feeds Component; each band carries one concrete input, output, and ownership statement.
options.risk: The reading order must remain obvious on mobile when the bands stack.

options.label: The decision case file
options.lineage: Technical change records and release-review packets
options.thesis: One token decision is treated as evidence: request, selected role, rejected alternatives, and release checks.
options.viewport: A large case header shows 'Primary next step' as the worked example; below it, a precise evidence trail proves why the semantic token is correct and the primitive is not.
options.risk: It is deliberately opinionated, so it must make the general rule visible before the reader reaches the catalog.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean documentation hero followed by grouped reference tables.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional docs page with a short introduction and a linear table sequence.
canonCard.risk: Clear but too close to the page you rejected.
